candidate_sentence_map.S1: TKM Grupp AS reported a weaker financial performance in 2025 amid difficult economic conditions and intense retail competition.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue declined 2.6% to €919.6 million from €944.6 million in 2024, while profit before tax fell 31.4% to €24.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Net profit decreased 36.1% to €17.5 million, reducing earnings per share from €0.67 to €0.43.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: EBITDA declined 14.7% to €77.4 million and operating profit fell from €47.6 million to €34.9 million, reducing the operating margin from 5% to 4% and the net margin from 3% to 2%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Gross margin nevertheless improved slightly from 27.5% to 27.7%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: The largest deterioration came from car trade.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Segment revenue fell 11.9% to €176.9 million, EBITDA declined 40.3% to €8.1 million and net profit fell 54.4% to €4.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: The report explicitly links this decline to Estonia’s motor vehicle tax, uncertainty before its introduction and reduced consumer confidence.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: New passenger-car sales in Estonia fell 48.6% for the year and 62.4% in the fourth quarter, although stronger markets in Latvia and Lithuania partly offset the decline.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Supermarket revenue was broadly stable, increasing 0.3% to €611.9 million, but net profit fell 38.6% to €9.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Lower sales volumes, increased promotional activity, weaker purchasing power and additional costs associated with the Jõgeva Selver renovation affected profitability.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Department-store revenue declined 1.1% to €103.0 million and the segment’s net loss widened to €0.5 million, while security revenue fell 8.1% to €20.1 million and the segment recorded a small loss.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Real estate was the main positive contributor: revenue increased 5.1% to €7.7 million and net profit rose 20.5% to €6.3 million, supported by logistics-centre rental income and lower borrowing costs, although the prior year included €4.0 million of one-off gains.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Cost control limited the impact of weaker sales.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Labour costs increased 3.7%, while other operating expenses rose only 0.2%.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Finance costs declined by €1.5 million, and income-tax expense fell by €1.2 million, supporting net profit.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Operating cash flow remained strong at €65.6 million, but cash declined to €29.5 million from €45.5 million after €25.5 million of investments and €26.5 million of dividends paid.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Strategic investments included new KIA and Škoda facilities, store refurbishments and digital-system upgrades.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: In January 2026, the Group agreed to acquire Rohe Auto, SKO Motors and a related real-estate company, subject to conditions, to expand its Škoda operations and strengthen the car segment.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: The proposed 2025 dividend is €0.60 per share, below the €0.65 paid for 2024.

evaluation.label: Yes
evaluation.justification: All key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered in S2 and S3 (revenue decline, profit before tax, net profit). K2 is covered in S6-S9 (car trade decline, Estonia tax impact, passenger car sales drop, offset by Latvia/Lithuania). K3 is covered in S10-S11 (supermarket revenue increase, profit decline, drivers). K4 is covered in S12 (department store revenue decline, net loss, warmer winter impact). K5 is covered in S13 (real estate revenue increase, profit decline, logistics centre rental income). K6 is covered in S17 (cash decrease, working capital, operating cash flow). K7 is covered in S18-S19 (car segment expansion, acquisitions, showroom construction). K8 is covered in S18 (refurbishments, digital upgrades). K9 is covered in S20 (dividend proposal). No material omissions affect overall understanding.
